issues_detected.description: The single erratum is internally self-referential: 'The June 2025 Data Release was published as a revision of the preceding June 2025 release'. related_datasets shows the June 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R) followed the March 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX), so the 'preceding' release should read March 2025. The change content (RGB immunofluorescent images, RO-Crate metadata corrections, naming convention change) is otherwise substantive and matches the related_datasets note for the June 2025 release.
issues_detected.recommendation: Correct the erratum to name the March 2025 release as the revised predecessor, or state explicitly which release the revision superseded.

issues_detected.description: Version ordering is inverted relative to release chronology: this June 2026 release carries version '2.0', while version_access records the earlier October 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM) and June 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R) as 'version 2.1'. A newer release with a lower version string will mislead any automated freshness comparison.
issues_detected.recommendation: State whether '2.0' is the Dataverse-assigned version of a distinct DOI series (in which case add a note that version strings are not comparable across DOIs) or correct the version to a value that increases monotonically with release date.

issues_detected.description: No processing documentation exists for the released data: preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools and imputation_protocols are all absent. The record documents the MuSIC pipeline in notes but states explicitly that computed cell maps are not in this release, so that tooling describes future output rather than the released files. At least one released artifact (cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_cell_atlas.zip) is a derived atlas whose construction is therefore undocumented.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add preprocessing_strategies (with used_software and versions) for each modality, in particular the alignment/demultiplexing and atlas-construction steps behind the perturb-seq cell atlas and the search/quantification steps behind the AP-MS and SEC-MS archives.

issues_detected.description: Distribution is documented only at the container level. Every one of the ten resources carries format 'ZIP' and media_type 'application/zip', with no statement of the scientific formats inside (mzML/mzTab, MTX/H5AD, OME-TIFF/PNG) and no character encoding anywhere in the record. A reuser can learn how large each archive is and how to verify it, but not what the archive will yield or whether it can be harmonized with other datasets.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record the inner formats and encodings per collection (e.g. mzML for SEC-MS/AP-MS, OME-TIFF for immunofluorescence, 10x MTX/H5AD for perturb-seq) so that format-based interoperability can be assessed without downloading multi-gigabyte archives.

issues_detected.description: No variable-level metadata: the `variables` slot is absent entirely, so no identifiers, units or definitions are supplied for any released table, channel or measurement.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add variables for at least the tabular outputs (perturb-seq atlas columns, mass-spectrometry result fields) with identifiers and descriptions.

issues_detected.description: Data-quality documentation is absent: anomalies, sampling_strategies and missing_data_documentation are all unpopulated. The extensive source_caveats blocks document disagreement between metadata sources, which is provenance hygiene about the record, not documentation of anomalies, outliers or missingness in the released measurements.
issues_detected.recommendation: Document known measurement-level quality issues per modality (failed wells/plates, low-confidence IF stains, dropout in single-cell data) and how missing values should be interpreted.

issues_detected.description: regulatory_restrictions carries only a negative statement ('FDA Regulated: No and Human Subjects: No') with no confidentiality_level, while confidential_elements records that perturb-seq data in KOLF2.1J and MDA-MB-468 are under temporary pre-publication embargo and third_party_sharing repeats that embargo. An access constraint that applies is therefore recorded outside the field a consumer would query for confidentiality classification.
issues_detected.recommendation: Set an explicit confidentiality_level and cross-reference the embargo from regulatory_restrictions so the classification is discoverable in one place.

issues_detected.description: publisher is recorded as the dataset landing-page URL, identical to `page`, rather than naming the publishing organization (University of Virginia Dataverse). The platform is recognizable from the URL and from the citation string, so the sub-element is satisfied, but the field value is a locator rather than an agent.
issues_detected.recommendation: Set publisher to the organization name (University of Virginia Dataverse), keeping the URL in `page`.

issues_detected.description: The record discloses a three-order-of-magnitude disagreement between its derived release total (12,601,718,300 bytes) and the project portal's stated 21.4 TB 'data volume', and correctly attributes the latter to the project rather than the release. Verified: the ten per-file byte values sum exactly to total_size_bytes and the per-collection totals reconcile, so the internal arithmetic is sound and the discrepancy is a scope difference, not an error.
issues_detected.recommendation: No correction needed; consider labelling the portal figure explicitly as project-cumulative to pre-empt misreading.

issues_detected.description: No named software produced or transformed the distributed data. The software that is named falls into non-qualifying roles: 10x Genomics 3'HT kit and the pipetting robot are capture/instrumentation; FAIRSCAPE is AI-readiness/metadata packaging; NDEx and the UVA Dataverse are hosting; and the MuSIC pipeline / Cell Mapping Toolkit / IMP are stated by the record itself to produce cell maps that are not in this release.
issues_detected.recommendation: Name the acquisition-to-release software with versions (e.g. CellRanger for perturb-seq, MaxQuant/DIA-NN or equivalent for the mass spectrometry archives, the image-processing chain for the IF archives) in used_software on the corresponding processing strategies.

issues_detected.description: future_use_impacts is absent, so no anticipated downstream social impact or mitigation analysis is offered, despite an Ethics module and two named ethics leads. known_biases carries a single representation-bias entry that gestures at generalizability but is not an impact analysis.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add future_use_impacts describing anticipated downstream effects of AI models trained on cell-line-derived maps and the mitigations the Ethics module envisages.

issues_detected.description: The immunofluorescence archives are the bulk of the release (12.6 GB of 12.6 GB) yet carry no content description. The record deliberately declines to import the October 2025 description because the MD5 checksums differ, and it records the 563-vs-464 protein-count disagreement rather than resolving it silently. This is defensible provenance discipline, but it leaves the largest component of the release semantically opaque.
issues_detected.recommendation: Obtain and record a first-party description and protein count for the June 2026 image archives.

semantic_insights: DOI 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C is well-formed and the 10.18130 prefix is the University of Virginia Dataverse, consistent with the publisher, page, citation and latest_version_doi, all of which agree on the same identifier.

Both NIH awards match NIH grant syntax: 1OT2OD032742-01 (OT2 activity code, OD institute) and 5U54HG012513-02 (U54, NHGRI), and the OT2 award is corroborated by a RePORTER core project number, application ID and project period.

Cell-line provenance is given with Cellosaurus RRIDs (RRID:CVCL_0419 for MDA-MB-468, RRID:CVCL_B5P3 for KOLF2.1J) plus donor context and MTA access route, which is the correct analogue of participant provenance for a non-human-subjects dataset.

Arithmetic is internally consistent and independently verifiable: the ten per-file byte values sum exactly to total_size_bytes (12,601,718,300), the per-collection file_count values sum to total_file_count (10), and each per-collection total_bytes equals its member sum.

All ten resources carry 32-hex-character MD5 checksums, and the record uses checksum difference as evidence that the June 2026 image archives are not the October 2025 files rather than inheriting a stale description.

The human-subjects chain is coherent throughout: involves_human_subjects=false, identifiable_elements_present=false, sensitive_elements_present=false, direct_collection.is_direct=false with cell-line sourcing, and informed_consent / participant_privacy / participant_compensation correctly absent rather than filled with vacuous text.

Licensing is consistent across three fields: the top-level `license` (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission (no_commercial_use), and ip_restrictions naming UCSD, Stanford and UCSF as the copyright holders for commercial re-licensing.

Version history is unusually complete for a beta release: five prior/current releases with DOIs, dates and what each changed, expressed both in version_access and as typed related_datasets relationships.
The record distinguishes release-level from project-level funding explicitly, attributing only 1OT2OD032742-01 to this deposit and marking the U54 and the Frederick Thomas Fund as project-level.

Limitations are typed and non-generic (scope, methodological, integration, coverage), including the admission that the PPI, localization and perturb-seq modalities interrogate incompletely overlapping protein sets — a substantive integration caveat.

Deliberate abstention is documented rather than hidden: a disputed protein count, a disputed author affiliation and an unsourced image description are each recorded with the ranking rule applied, which is stronger provenance discipline than a confident single value would be.

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; raw_data_sources cite RRID:CVCL_0419 and RRID:CVCL_B5P3.
sub_elements.quality_note: A single persistent identifier is used consistently as id, doi, citation target and latest-version pointer, with no divergence between them.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Format 10.XXXX/... satisfied. Prefix 10.18130 is the University of Virginia Dataverse, which matches the publisher, page host and citation repository, so the prefix is plausible rather than merely well-formed. Cell-line RRIDs use the Cellosaurus CVCL namespace and are correctly formed.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description enumerates the four modalities (Perturb-seq, SEC-MS, AP-MS, immunofluorescence), the two cell systems (MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J iPSC and derivatives) and the treatment/differentiation conditions covered by each.
sub_elements.quality_note: Description is well over 200 characters and is specific about which modality covers which cell state, so a reader can tell before download what is and is not in the release.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Description content matches keywords, subsets, subpopulations.distribution and file_collections; no modality is named in the description that is missing from the file listing, and none is listed that the description omits.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: 28 terms including AP-MS, SEC-MS, perturb-seq, CRISPR/Cas9, MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J, paclitaxel, vorinostat, protein-protein interaction, subcellular imaging, Bridge2AI, CM4AI.
sub_elements.quality_note: Far exceeds the five-keyword threshold and spans domain, assay, cell line, perturbagen and program, including both abbreviations and expansions (SEC-MS / size exclusion chromatography) which aids retrieval.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Every keyword is instantiated somewhere in the record; none is aspirational. Program context (Bridge2AI, CM4AI) is inferred from the keywords and funders values themselves.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; file_collections gives five named collections each containing resources with id, name, format, bytes, md5 and issued date.
sub_elements.quality_note: The landing page resolves through the same DOI as the identifier, and the hierarchical resource structure is complete down to per-file checksums and sizes.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: URL is well-formed and the persistentId parameter matches the doi field exactly.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: seven entries with relationship_type values is_new_version_of (four prior CM4AI releases), is_described_by (bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/2024.05.21.589311), is_referenced_by (perturbation atlas preprint) and references (Nature 10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3).
sub_elements.quality_note: Relationships are typed and each carries a note explaining what the target contains and how it differs, e.g. the October 2025 release lacking AP-MS data.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: parent_datasets is absent, but the four is_new_version_of links supply the lineage that field would carry, and each target DOI is well-formed (three Dataverse, three bioRxiv, one Nature).

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms spells out CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 with the share/adapt permissions and the Attribution, NonCommercial and ShareAlike conditions, and states that commercial use requires separate negotiation with UCSD, Stanford and/or UCSF; data_use_permission: no_commercial_use; ip_restrictions names the Regents of the University of California and the Board of Trustees of Stanford as copyright holders, with spatial proteomics raw images carved out to Stanford.
sub_elements.quality_note: Not a bare licence label: the permissions, the conditions, the per-data-package copyright split and the route to a commercial licence are all stated.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The three licensing fields agree (top-level license, license_terms, data_use_permission), and the ip_restrictions copyright split is consistent with data_collectors placing imaging at Stanford and mass spectrometry at UCSF.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance: 'The release records FDA Regulated: No and Human Subjects: No.'; data_governance.committee_name: 'Data Governance Committee' with committee_contact Jillian Parker (ORCID:0000-0003-4535-3486, jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu) and an access_review_process describing Data Access Committee supervision and dual-licensing negotiation; confidential_elements records the pre-publication embargo on perturb-seq data.
sub_elements.quality_note: The regulatory statement itself is thin, but the sub-element's scope includes governance contacts, and a named, ORCID-identified, emailable governance contact plus a described access-review process is actionable information a requester can act on today.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: confidentiality_level and hipaa_compliant are unset. HIPAA is genuinely inapplicable to de-identified cell-line data, but the embargo recorded in confidential_elements is a real access constraint that is not reflected in the confidentiality classification field; logged as a low-severity consistency issue rather than a failure, since the constraint is documented elsewhere in the record.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats.access_urls: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, with notes: 'Individual file download is available; the dataset as a whole exceeds the repository's 1.9 GB ZIP download limit, and the Data Access API is offered for programmatic access.'
sub_elements.quality_note: The dedicated download_url slot is unpopulated, but the sub-element asks for direct download links or platform access instructions and the record gives the latter with the operationally important detail — bulk ZIP download will fail at 1.9 GB, so use per-file download or the API.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Access URL is well-formed and resolves through the same persistentId as doi and page. Scored on the access instructions, which are non-trivial and specific to this release's size; the absence of a per-file direct URL is noted as a gap, not a failure.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: format ZIP, media_type application/zip; each of the ten resources carries format: ZIP, media_type: application/zip, compression: zip and a file_type of data_file, image_file or metadata_file.
sub_elements.quality_note: Formats and MIME types are stated for every distributed object without exception, and file_type distinguishes image, data and metadata payloads.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: media_type application/zip is the correct MIME type for the stated format, and is consistent across all ten resources. Only the container format is given; the inner scientific formats are unstated, which is recorded as a warning here and carried into Element 3 sub-element 2 where format standardization for reuse is the question.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets (seven typed links) plus external_resources (seven entries: cm4ai.org portal, MassIVE deposits for SEC-MS and AP-MS, Figshare CRISPRi atlas, FAIRSCAPE at fairscape.github.io, Cell Mapping Toolkit at github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline with readthedocs, IMP at integrativemodeling.org, NDEx at ndexbio.org), each flagged archival true/false.
sub_elements.quality_note: External resources are separated into archival deposits and non-archival tooling/documentation, which tells a reuser which links are citable mirrors of the data and which are project infrastructure.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The MassIVE and Figshare deposits named in external_resources match the mirrors described in third_party_sharing, and both record the perturb-seq embargo consistently.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met: distribution_formats is populated with access_urls, page/publisher link to a UVA Dataverse deposit, and the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence explicitly permits share and adapt.
sub_elements.evidence: license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; license_and_use_terms.license_terms grants share and adapt rights under Attribution, NonCommercial and ShareAlike with 'no additional restrictions', and states the citation expectation for derived publications.
sub_elements.quality_note: Reuse is affirmatively permitted for non-commercial purposes with a stated route (separate negotiation) for commercial reuse, so both categories of prospective user know where they stand.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 with a canonical licence URL; the NonCommercial term is consistent with data_use_permission: no_commercial_use and with the ip_restrictions commercial-licensing clause.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (see sub-element 1).
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: format ZIP / media_type application/zip only; file_collections.resources all carry format ZIP; no `encoding` value appears anywhere in the record; no inner format is named for the mass-spectrometry, imaging or single-cell payloads.
sub_elements.quality_note: The only format documented is a compression container. A reuser planning harmonization cannot tell whether the SEC-MS archives contain mzML or vendor raw files, whether the images are OME-TIFF or PNG, or whether the perturb-seq atlas is MTX, H5AD or CSV — which is precisely the information this sub-element exists to supply.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Scored separately from Element 2 sub-element 4 by design: that item asks whether distribution formats are specified (ZIP with MIME type answers it), while this item asks whether formats are standardized for reuse and integration, where a container plus no encoding answers nothing. Not a case of missing fields but of insufficient content.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (see sub-element 1).
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: RO-Crate; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset. instances additionally carry Bridge2AI controlled-vocabulary codes (B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:63, B2AI_TOPIC:15/26/34).
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is stated at three levels — packaging standard, metadata schema with a resolvable w3id URI, and schema class — and is corroborated by a shipped cm4ai_release_metadata.zip and by errata describing RO-Crate metadata corrections in a prior release.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: RO-Crate is a genuine community packaging standard and the w3id schema URI is well-formed; the ontology term prefixes are used consistently across instances.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (see sub-element 1).
sub_elements.evidence: No `variables` entries anywhere in the record.
sub_elements.quality_note: No variable identifiers, definitions, units or value ranges are provided for any released artifact, including the perturb-seq cell atlas and the mass-spectrometry result tables, so no field-level reuse is possible from the metadata alone.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Consistent with is_tabular: false at the dataset level, but the release nonetheless contains tabular derivatives (a cell atlas), so is_tabular does not excuse the absence.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: four entries with use_category and usage_notes (AI-ready functional genomics data, AI model training, cellular process analysis, perturbation/treatment response analysis); prohibited_uses: clinical decision-making and patient care, with prohibition_reason citing absent regulatory oversight and the laboratory cell-line origin; discouraged_uses: use as a source of computed cell maps, which this release does not contain.
sub_elements.quality_note: All three registers are populated and each is reasoned rather than asserted; the discouraged use is unusually precise and matches the stated scope limitation.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Prohibited and discouraged uses are consistent with known_limitations (interim release, no predicted cell maps) and with human_subject_research (non-clinical laboratory data); no intended use contradicts the NonCommercial licence.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition fails on external evidence (description and keywords name cell lines MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2.1J, not participants; collection_mechanisms from E8 describes a pipetting robot, a CRISPR lentiviral library and the 10x 3'HT kit, not recruitment). The governance disjunct carries this sub-element: E2 evidence shows a governance constraint that applies — data_governance names a Data Governance Committee with an emailable contact and an access_review_process under which a Data Access Committee supervises distribution and dual licensing, and ip_restrictions requires separate negotiation for commercial use. Per #1060 this is a constraint that applies, not a record that none does, and it is exactly the 'donor-derived material, a data access committee, an ethics contact' case the governance disjunct exists for.
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two entries, each with review_details ('supervise ethical matters relating to dataset preparation, licensing, dissemination and Data Access') and a named contact_person — Vardit Ravitsky (ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801, ravitskyv@thehastingscenter.org) and Jean-Christophe Bélisle-Pipon (ORCID:0000-0002-8965-8153, jean-christophe_belisle-pipon@sfu.ca); human_subject_research records the Dataverse determination (Human Subjects: No, De-identified Samples: Yes, FDA Regulated: No) with the preprint's reasoning; data_governance.stewardship_roles describes the Ethics module's remit.
sub_elements.quality_note: Oversight is documented in the form appropriate to a cell-line dataset: no IRB protocol exists to cite, but the responsible parties are named, identified and contactable, their remit is defined, and the no-human-subjects determination is attributed to the source that made it.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Consistency check passes: involves_human_subjects=false, so the rule requiring IRB detail when it is true does not fire. data_protection_impacts is absent, which is defensible where no personal data are processed. The record flags its own uncertainty honestly — source_caveats notes the preprint describes the Data Access Committee in the future tense as a plan while the release uses the label 'Data Governance Committee'.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same governance disjunct as sub-element 1: E2 data_governance and ip_restrictions state access and licensing constraints that apply, and the material is donor-derived (raw_data_sources describes a 51-year-old female donor's pleural effusion and a Northern European male iPSC donor). The human-subjects condition itself fails on E1/E8 evidence.
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false; deidentification_details: 'Samples are recorded as de-identified. Data were derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines; the underlying cell lines are described as ethically sourced.' human_subject_research.notes adds the basis: data 'are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject.'
sub_elements.quality_note: No formal method label (Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, k-anonymity) is given, and none applies — no identifiers were stripped by these creators because the material arrived de-identified from ATCC and HipSci. What the record supplies instead is the correct answer to the underlying question: the identifiability status, the source of that status, and the reasoning behind it.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Method appropriateness check passes for the data type: cell-line-derived proteomic, imaging and transcriptomic measurements carry no direct identifiers, and the record does not over-claim any de-identification procedure it did not perform. Consistent with sensitive_elements_present: false and with the absence of participant_privacy.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition not met on external evidence: description and keywords (E1) name cell lines and assays, never participants or patients as subjects of this dataset; collection_mechanisms (E8) describes robotic fixation, a CRISPR lentiviral library and 10x single-cell chemistry, with no recruitment; direct_collection.is_direct is false, stating data came from commercially available and repository-sourced cell lines rather than from human subjects. Per #1060 the governance disjunct does not reach this sub-element: a Data Governance Committee, an embargo and a commercial-licensing clause are governance structures, not participants.
sub_elements.evidence: participant_privacy and participant_privacy.reidentification_risk are absent; there are no participants in this dataset whose privacy could be protected or whose re-identification risk could be assessed.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. Scoring 0 here would measure the dataset's subject matter rather than the quality of its documentation; the record's related claim — that samples cannot be matched to a human subject with current knowledge — is credited under sub-element 2 where it belongs.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition not met on the same external E1/E8 evidence: no participants are described in description or keywords, and collection_mechanisms documents laboratory procedures rather than recruitment or enrolment. The governance disjunct does not extend to participant-facing sub-elements (#1060).
sub_elements.evidence: informed_consent absent. No participants were enrolled by this project; cell lines were obtained from ATCC and from HipSci under a material transfer agreement.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. Consent for the original donations sits with the source repositories, and the record does not falsely claim to have obtained consent it did not obtain.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition not met on the same external E1/E8 evidence. No population was enrolled, so no at-risk population could be protected and no participant could be compensated; subpopulations states explicitly that 'Subpopulations in this dataset are cell lines and differentiation states rather than human demographic groups'.
sub_elements.evidence: at_risk_populations and participant_compensation absent.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. The record's own statement that its subpopulations are cell states rather than demographic groups is the clearest possible evidence that this question has no referent here.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: subpopulations: subpopulation_elements_present true, with identification naming MDA-MB-468 (untreated, paclitaxel, vorinostat) and KOLF2.1J (undifferentiated, NPC, neuron, cardiomyocyte), and a distribution statement giving modality coverage per group; subsets: two entries with is_subpopulation: true and descriptions of which modalities each contains.
sub_elements.quality_note: The distribution statement is the substantive part: it says which modality covers which cell state, so a user can see that AP-MS covers treated MDA-MB-468 only and IF covers MDA-MB-468 only. The record also correctly reframes 'subpopulation' for a cell-line dataset rather than leaving the field empty or forcing human demographics into it.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Coverage claims in subpopulations.distribution match the file_collections listing exactly (AP-MS: two treated archives; IF: three MDA-MB-468 archives; SEC-MS: KOLF2 and MDA-MB-468; perturb-seq: KOLF2 atlas and raw). Note one internal tension: the description says perturb-seq covers MDA-MB-468 with and without treatment, but the release ships only KOLF2 perturb-seq archives, with MDA-MB-468 perturb-seq listed as embargoed in third_party_sharing — the record's embargo note reconciles this.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: total_file_count: 10; total_size_bytes: 12601718300; each file_collection reports file_count and total_bytes (AP-MS 2/249100, IF 3/12600000000, SEC-MS 2/265700, perturb-seq 2/103500, metadata 1/1100000); subsets carry is_data_split: false; source_caveats derives the total from the per-file listing and states the rounding basis.
sub_elements.quality_note: Concrete, verifiable counts are reported at the distribution level with an explicit derivation, and the split flags are set. Scored 1 on that basis, but with a real gap noted: no measurement-level counts (cells profiled, guides, images, proteins imaged) are given, and the record deliberately declines to state a protein count because its sources disagree (563 vs 464) and neither figure is attributable to these files.

sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Collection-identified condition met (acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms are both populated) and datasets-shared condition met (distribution_formats with access URLs, Dataverse landing page, reuse-permitting licence).

No mechanism is described for the SEC-MS or AP-MS chromatography and purification steps, which are covered only at the acquisition_methods level.

sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same as sub-element 1.

This matters concretely: cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_cell_atlas.zip is a derived atlas, and the AP-MS and SEC-MS archives are results rather than instrument output, so real processing occurred and is entirely unstated. instances.label: false is set for the imaging instance, but no labeling procedure is described.

Scored 0 on total absence of the named evidence, not on insufficiency.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Element 8's datasets-shared condition is met and the release contains processed artifacts (a derived cell atlas, mass-spectrometry results), so the dataset was processed at all. Per #1081 this sub-element is not gated on whether a repository is pointed at — gating it on the pointer would let silence excuse the question.

Software named elsewhere: the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit and a pipetting robot (collection_mechanisms); FAIRSCAPE AI-readiness framework (external_resources); the Cell Mapping Toolkit / MuSIC pipeline at github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline and the IMP package (external_resources, plus the notes pipeline description); NDEx and the UVA Dataverse (external_resources, publisher).

Each named tool falls in a non-qualifying role: the 10x kit and the pipetting robot are capture and instrumentation (a); NDEx and Dataverse are hosting and serving (b); FAIRSCAPE is AI-readiness packaging and provenance metadata production (c); and the MuSIC pipeline, Cell Mapping Toolkit and IMP fall under (e) — the record itself states these produce cell maps that are not in this release. Naming the capture chemistry prominently neither adds to nor subtracts from the answer.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (see sub-element 1).
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: four is_new_version_of links to prior CM4AI releases, is_described_by to the CM4AI bioRxiv preprint (doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311), is_referenced_by to the perturbation atlas preprint (doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734, PMCID PMC11580897), and references to Schaffer et al., Nature 642:222-231 (doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3).

strengths: Identifier and citation infrastructure is coherent end to end: one DOI (10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, a valid UVA Dataverse prefix) serves as id, doi, landing page parameter, citation target and latest_version_doi, with five prior releases each independently resolvable.

Provenance discipline is exceptional: the record documents where its sources disagree (563 vs 464 proteins imaged, a conflicting author affiliation, 21.4 TB portal figure vs a 12.6 GB derived release total), states the ranking rule it applied, and declines to import an image description from a prior release whose MD5 checksums differ.
Internal arithmetic is verifiable and correct: ten per-file byte values sum exactly to total_size_bytes, per-collection counts sum to total_file_count, and every resource carries a well-formed MD5.

Funding transparency is above the norm — two NIH awards in valid NIH syntax with RePORTER application ID, supplement number, award amount and project period, and an explicit distinction between funding recorded on this release and project-level funding acknowledged in the preprint.

Ethics and governance are documented in the form appropriate to a non-human-subjects, cell-line dataset: named ethics leads with ORCIDs and emails, a named governance contact, a described access-review and dual-licensing process, and a de-identification status attributed to the source that determined it.
Use guidance is complete across all three registers (intended, prohibited, discouraged) and each is reasoned, with the discouraged use precisely matching the release's stated scope limitation.
weaknesses: No processing documentation for the released data at all: preprocessing, cleaning, labeling, annotation and imputation slots are empty, and no software that produced or transformed the distributed files is named — the tools that are named are capture, hosting, metadata-packaging, or (by the record's own statement) producers of outputs not in this release.

Formats are documented only as ZIP containers with no inner scientific formats and no character encoding anywhere, so the largest barrier to reuse — knowing what a 4.6 GB archive will yield — is left standing.
